```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(syinexplore)
```

## Who is this app for?

Trash Wheel Explorer is for environmental volunteers and readers
interested in cleaner waterways.

It helps users investigate this question:

**At selected Baltimore Trash Wheels and times, which rubbish
categories have the highest estimated item counts per recorded
collection?**

Choose collection sites and years, then compare the chart, table
and written results.

## Install the package

Run these commands in your R console. Installation requires
an internet connection.

```r
install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github(
  "ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-syin0014-cloud"
)
```

## Launch the app

After installation, run:

```r
library(syinexplore)

run_app()
```

The app opens in a browser or the RStudio Viewer. It uses data
included in the installed package, so it does not download a CSV
when it starts.

To stop the app in RStudio, click Stop in the Console or press Esc.

## Choose collection records

- **Trash Wheels:** choose one or more collection devices.
  Selecting several shows them in separate chart panels.
- **Collection years:** move the two slider handles to choose
  the first and last years. Both end years are included.

Results update automatically when either selection changes.

Start with Mister Trash Wheel and 2022–2023. Then change the year
range to explore whether the average counts and leading rubbish
categories change. Select another Trash Wheel to compare its records.

## Read the results

The text above the chart identifies the rubbish categories with
the highest mean counts for each selected Trash Wheel.

Longer bars represent higher estimated item counts per recorded
collection. The chart panels use the same horizontal scale.

The table contains:

- **Trash Wheel:** the device that collected the rubbish.
- **Rubbish type:** one of seven categories in the source data.
  The app calls polystyrene "Foam items".
- **Collections:** all selected collection records for that category.
- **Recorded collections:** selected records with a reported item count.
- **Mean items:** the average estimated item count among those
  recorded collections.

Check Recorded collections before comparing means, because reporting
coverage can differ across categories.

"Not recorded" means no counts were reported for that group.
It does not mean zero. Missing counts are excluded from the mean.

Collection counts repeat across rubbish categories. Do not add
the category rows together to count distinct collections.

## Reproduce a summary in R

You can use the package's summary function without opening the app:

```{r}
#| label: example-summary

example_summary <- summarise_data(
  data = trash_items,
  wheels = "Mister Trash Wheel",
  years = c(2022, 2023)
)

example_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    trash_type = gsub("_", " ", trash_type)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    trash_type,
    recorded_collections,
    mean_count
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c(
      "Rubbish type",
      "Recorded collections",
      "Mean items"
    )
  )
```

The rows are ordered from the highest mean to the lowest.
The first row therefore identifies the category with the highest
average count for this selection.

These values describe items per recorded collection.
They are not yearly totals or measures of environmental harm.

## What if there are no matching records?

If you remove all Trash Wheels, the app asks you to select at least one.

To try a selection with no records, choose Gwynnda Trash Wheel
and 2014–2015. The app explains that no records match and suggests
changing the years or selecting another device.

If only some selected devices have records, the coverage message
identifies those without records. No matching records does not mean
that the device collected zero rubbish.

## Keep the limits in mind

Item counts are estimates based on sampling.

A mean per collection helps compare records without relying only
on total collection counts. However, it does not account for all
differences in collection conditions, locations or reporting coverage.

A higher mean does not by itself show a more polluted location or
a better-performing machine. Item counts also do not measure how
harmful each rubbish category is.

This historical dataset covers 2014–2023. It does not show current
collection totals or all rubbish remaining in the waterways.

## Data sources

The data were distributed by
[TidyTuesday on 5 March 2024](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2024/2024-03-05).

The original project is
[Baltimore Healthy Harbor / Mr. Trash Wheel](https://www.mrtrashwheel.com/).
